caption: How hi net expose works. A service runs on your machine, such as a web app on port 3000. hi net expose asks NetBird's reverse proxy for a public HTTPS address that leads through the NetBird network to that port, with a lock in front: a generated password by default, or a PIN, the key in the link, NetBird SSO groups, or none. The address ends on its own after a while, or when you stop it.

items.title: localhost:3000
items.does: A web app, a webhook receiver, a notebook, or an API. It needs no changes.

items.title: hi-aiw9-3000-k2x7
items.does: Prints the address and its password, logs each request, and ends at `--for` or Ctrl+C.

items.title: https://hi-aiw9-3000-k2x7.eu1.netbird.services
items.does: Visitors arrive here, pass the lock (a password, a PIN, the key in the link, SSO groups, or `--public`), and reach your service through NetBird.

key.text: On NetBird; nothing on it opens a port to the internet.
What you share, as it already runs.
Asks for the address, keeps it while it lasts, and shows who comes in.
NetBird's, with the lock in front, so visitors never reach your machine directly.
